West
WEST
n. and adj. (rendering Hebrew yām and ma'arāb, Greek dusmē)
From Old English west, cognate with Latin vesper, evening — the west being the quarter of the day's decline. The Hebrew is startlingly concrete: the ordinary word for west is yām, the sea, because for a man standing in Canaan the west simply is the Mediterranean. To say westward in Hebrew is to say seaward. The alternative ma'arāb means the place of the sun's going in, its setting.

Biblical Definition

West in Scripture is the seaward side, the quarter of the sun's setting, and above all the far end of the axis on which God measures both His mercy and the reach of His gathering. Because Israel's west was the open sea, the word carried the sense of the boundary beyond which the land gave out — the uttermost sea marked the western limit of the promise. The compass is used most memorably as a pair: “As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us” (Psa 103:12), where the two ends of an infinite line stand for a separation between the believer and his sin which no measurement can close. The same pairing then becomes the shape of the gathering of the elect from among the nations. To Israel God promises, “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west” (Isa 43:5); and Jacob is told his descendants shall “spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed” (Gen 28:14). The Lord Jesus takes up the same figure and turns it against presumption: “many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven” (Mat 8:11) — strangers from the far quarters seated at the patriarchs' table while the children of the kingdom are cast out.

Webster 1828 Definition

The point of the compass where the sun sets; in Hebrew idiom the seaward quarter, the Mediterranean lying west of Canaan; and in Scripture one end of the measure of pardon and one quarter from which the redeemed are gathered.

expand to see more

WEST, n. 1. That point of the horizon where the sun sets at the equinox; the point opposite to the east.

2. The region of the heavens or of the earth lying toward the setting sun; the occident.

3. adj. Being in a line toward the setting sun; as the west border, the west side.

4. In Hebrew usage, the sea; the Mediterranean lying westward of Canaan, whence seaward and westward are one word.

5. In Scripture, as far as the east is from the west. Psalm 103. Many shall come from the east and west. Matt. 8.

Key Scripture

Psalm 103:12 — "As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us."

Isaiah 43:5 — "Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west;"

Genesis 28:14 — "And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed."

Matthew 8:11 — "And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven."

Modern Corruption

The gathering from east and west is read as a promise that all men are saved regardless of repentance and faith, emptying the very sayings in which Christ warns that the children of the kingdom may be cast out.

expand to see more

The sayings about the gathering from east and west are among the most misused in the Gospels. Because they announce that strangers from every quarter will sit down with Abraham, they are offered as evidence of a final inclusion so wide that repentance and faith become optional and hell empties. The context forbids it flatly. Mat 8:11 is spoken in commendation of a centurion's faith — I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel — and the very next verse continues, but the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness. The saying is not a promise that everyone comes in; it is a warning that descent and religious proximity save nobody while faith brings outsiders to the table. To quote the first half as universalism is to reverse the plain intent of the whole.

The second corruption is subtler and pastoral rather than doctrinal: treating Psa 103:12 as a comforting exaggeration rather than as a measured statement of fact. The psalmist is precise. He does not say our transgressions are removed as far as north is from south, and the omission is deliberate, for north and south meet at the poles and the distance between them can be stated. East and west have no meeting point; travel east forever and you never arrive at west. That is the distance the verse asserts, and it is asserted of a real removal accomplished at real cost. The believer troubled by a sin long ago confessed is not being soothed by a figure of speech; he is being told the location of his guilt, which is nowhere the LORD is willing to look for it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yām means sea, and by orientation west, since the Mediterranean lay westward of Canaan; ma'arāb is the place of the sun's entering, its setting. Greek dusmē is a setting or sinking, used in the plural for the west.

expand to see more

Hebrew yām (H3220) — sea; and by the geography of Canaan, the west or seaward side; the uttermost sea is the western limit of the land (Deu 11:24).

Hebrew ma'arāb (H4628) — the going in of the sun, the west quarter; from 'ārab, to grow dark or become evening.

Greek dusmē (G1424) — a setting, of the sun; used in the plural for the west, as in from the east and west (Mat 8:11).

Hebrew 'acha'rōn — hinder, behind; the western sea is the hinder sea, the observer facing east so that west lies at his back.

The compass pair — east and west form the one axis with no terminus, which is why Psa 103:12 chooses it and not north and south to measure the removal of sin.

Usage

"Of the measure of pardon: as far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us (Psa 103:12)."

"Of the gathering of the redeemed: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west (Isa 43:5)."

"Of outsiders seated and insiders cast out: many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham (Mat 8:11)."
